info.title: PostQueen Public API
info.description:
Schedule posts, upload media, read analytics and manage the channels of your PostQueen workspace.

## Authentication

Send your API key in the `Authorization` header exactly as it is, with no prefix:

```
Authorization: YOUR_API_KEY
```

The key is under **Connections > API Keys** in the app. Only a workspace Admin or Super Admin can reveal or rotate it. An app your users sign in to with OAuth sends its `pos_` access token in the same header, also with no prefix. The workspace needs a subscription, and the free trial counts.

## Rate limits

`POST /posts` has an hourly limit per workspace. `POST /upload` and `POST /upload-from-url` allow 300 requests an hour each, per workspace. Nothing else is limited. A limited endpoint answers with `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers, and over the limit with `429` and `Retry-After` (seconds).

## Terminology

The app says channel, the API says integration. They are the same thing: a connected account on a network.

Starts connecting a network and returns the URL of its sign-in page, for a person to open in a browser. When they approve, the new channel appears in the workspace and they land in the PostQueen app.

This works for networks that sign in with their own consent page. Networks connected with a handle, key or password (Bluesky, DEV, Hashnode, Lemmy, Listmonk, Moltbook, Nostr, WordPress) answer 200 with a `url` that is only an internal state value: connect those from **Add Channel** in the app. A network marked Soon on [Channels](/channels/overview) cannot be connected yet, whatever this returns. The sign-in state is kept for one hour.

get.description:
What a post to this channel may carry: the network's rules in words, the maximum text length, the JSON schema of its `settings`, and the tools you can run with Trigger a tool. `settings` is the text `No additional settings required` for networks without a settings schema.

Moltbook answers `No additional settings required`, but Create a post needs `submolt` for it.

parameters.description: The channel's id, from List channels

settings.description: JSON schema of the provider settings, or the string "No additional settings required"

output.rules: Bluesky can have maximum 1 video or 4 pictures in one post, it can also be without attachments

post.description: Runs one of a network's helper tools on a channel, such as listing WordPress post types or Hashnode publications, to get the ids a post's `settings` need. Get a channel's settings lists each channel's tools with their `methodName` and `dataSchema`. The tools of every network are on [Provider tools](/public-api/integrations/provider-tools).

delete.description: Deletes a channel and, first, every post of that channel in PostQueen, whatever its state: scheduled, drafts, published records and failed posts. Pending publishing for them is canceled. Posts of other channels are not touched, and nothing already published is taken down from the network. Connecting the account again does not bring the posts back.

post.description:
Schedules, publishes or saves posts on one or more channels. Each entry in `posts` is one channel: its text, media, thread and the network's `settings`. PostQueen checks every entry before it saves anything: the body and each network's required settings always, and for everything but a draft also the network's rules on length and media.

The settings of each network are on [Posting settings by network](/public-api/providers/overview).

value.content: Drag a post to move it. Hold Shift to copy it.

two-channels.summary: One post on two channels (Bluesky and Nostr)

value.content: The calendar now shows drafts next to scheduled posts.

## Why we rebuilt the calendar

Three things changed.
Idea: a post about the calendar.

put.description: Moves a post between draft and scheduled. `schedule` queues it for its stored date. A draft is checked first, with the same rules [Create a post](/public-api/posts/create) applies to a scheduled post: text or media present, the network's required settings, its media rules and its length. A draft that fails answers 400 with the channel name and the reason, and stays a draft. `draft` stops any pending publish and keeps the post as a draft. The date does not change. Published and failed posts cannot change.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The post's id

draftCheck.summary: A draft that fails its checks

put.description:
Merges the keys you pass into the post's existing provider settings. Only those keys change: the content, the publish date and the post ids stay as they are.

Works on posts that have not been published yet, meaning a scheduled post (`QUEUE`) whose publish time is still ahead, or a draft. The merged settings go through the same validation as creating a post, except on a draft, where only the empty-content check runs.

Pass the id of the main post, not of a comment in its thread.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The post's id

settings.description: Provider settings to merge into the post's existing settings. Only the keys you pass change. Keys depend on the channel's platform, and `__type` is always taken from the channel.

400.description: The id belongs to a comment (pass the main post's id), the post was already published or failed, its publish time has passed, or the merged settings failed validation

example.message: Only scheduled posts that were not published yet (or drafts) can be updated

post.description:
Uploads a file to the media library, as multipart form data in a field named `file`. PostQueen reads the type from the file itself: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, TIFF, MP4 or MOV, up to 1 GB. A video comes back `processing` while it is prepared in the background (a MOV becomes an MP4): poll Get media status until it is `ready`, then use the `path` that returns.

A post takes media whose path ends in .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp or .mp4, so an AVIF, BMP or TIFF file can be stored but not posted.

400.description: `No file provided`, `Unsupported file type.`, or `File size exceeds the maximum allowed size of 1073741824 bytes.`

post.description: PostQueen downloads a file from a public HTTPS URL into the media library. The URL's path must end in .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp or .mp4 (a query string is ignored), and it cannot point at a private or local address. The download may take up to 5 minutes and 1 GB, and the type is then read from the file itself. A video comes back `processing`, as with Upload a file.

url.description: URL of the file to upload

400.description: The URL failed validation (`message` is a list), or `Failed to fetch URL`, `File is too large.` or `Unsupported file type.` (`msg`)

message: URL must be a public HTTPS URL and cannot point to internal network addresses

get.description: Whether an uploaded file is ready to put on a post. A video answers the upload endpoints with `status: "processing"` and is ready a few seconds to a few minutes later, possibly with a new `path`. Use the `path` this returns once `status` is `ready`. `failed` carries the reason in `processingError`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The media id from an upload

get.description:
Checks an OAuth app and returns what PostQueen shows on its consent screen. You do not normally call this: send the person to the consent page at `https://app.postqueen.ai/oauth/authorize` with the same query, and that page calls it. It is useful to check a `client_id`.

Outside `/public/v1`; takes no API key. A client registered with Register a client must also send one of its `redirect_uri`s, and a public client (no secret) must send a PKCE `code_challenge` with method `S256`.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: The app's client id: `pca_...` for an app made under Connections > Developers, `pcd_...` for a registered client

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: Must be `code`. No other response type is supported.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: An opaque value echoed back in the response and in the redirect to your app. Use a random value to protect against CSRF.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Required for a registered client, and must be one of its `redirect_uris`. An app made under Connections > Developers always uses its stored Redirect URL

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: PKCE challenge. Required for a registered client without a secret

parameters.name: code_challenge_method
parameters.description: PKCE method. A registered client must use `S256`

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Accepted and not used; the granted scope comes back on the token response

name.description: App name shown on the consent screen

description.description: App description shown on the consent screen

picture.description: The app's profile picture, or null when none is set. Use `picture.path` as the image URL.

redirectUrl.description: Where PostQueen sends the user after they approve or deny

state.description: The `state` you sent, echoed back. Absent if you did not send one.

400.description: `Invalid client_id`, `Invalid redirect_uri`, `code_challenge is required for this client`, `Only the S256 code_challenge_method is supported`, or a failed query validation

post.description:
Exchanges the code from your callback for a `pos_` access token. Call it from your server. Send the client secret in the body, or the id and secret as HTTP Basic in `Authorization`. A public client registered with `token_endpoint_auth_method: none` sends no secret and proves itself with `code_verifier`. The code works once, for 10 minutes.

The token does not expire. It stops working when the person revokes the app under **Connections > Approved Apps**, when they leave the workspace, are disabled or delete their account, or when they approve the app again (the new token replaces it). Send it in `Authorization` with no prefix on `/public/v1`. Outside `/public/v1`; takes no API key.

code.description: The authorization code from your callback URL

client_id.description: Your app's Client ID. Leave it out when you send it in a Basic Authorization header

client_secret.description: Your app's Client Secret (starts with `pcs_`). Leave it out with Basic auth, or for a public PKCE client

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier, required when the authorization request carried a code_challenge

redirect_uri.description: Required when the authorization request carried one, and must match it

id.description: The workspace the person approved your app for

cus.description: The workspace's billing customer id, or null

access_token.description: The token to send in the `Authorization` header (starts with `pos_`)

token_type.description: Always `bearer`. On `/public/v1` send the token with no prefix all the same

scope.description: Granted scopes: `mcp:read mcp:write`, plus `openid email` for clients allowed email claims

400.description: `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_grant` (a wrong, used or expired code, a wrong `code_verifier` or `redirect_uri`), or a failed body validation

401.description: `invalid_client`: unknown client id, or a wrong or missing secret

post.description:
Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591). A client, usually an MCP client, registers itself and gets a `pcd_` client id without anyone making an app under Connections > Developers. Callbacks must be https, an http loopback address (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`) or a private-use scheme such as `cursor://`. Only the `authorization_code` grant is supported. Send `token_endpoint_auth_method: none` for a public client, which then gets no secret and must use PKCE (`S256`). A registered client that nobody has approved after 30 days may be removed.

Outside `/public/v1`; takes no API key.

redirect_uris.description: The callback URLs the client may use

client_name.description: The name shown on the consent screen, up to 100 characters. Default `MCP Client`

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: `none` for a public client with PKCE. Anything else gets a secret; the default is `client_secret_post`

scope.description: Accepted; the scope is set by PostQueen

201.description: Registered. `client_secret` is present only for a confidential client, and is shown once

example.error_description: redirect_uris must use https or a private-use scheme (http is allowed for loopback only)

ApiKeyAuth.name: Authorization
ApiKeyAuth.description: Your API key from Connections > API Keys, or an OAuth access token (`pos_...`). Send it as it is, with no `Bearer` prefix.

disabled.description: True when the channel is switched off in the app. A disabled channel does not publish

customer.description: The customer the channel is assigned to. Left out when there is none

originalName.description: The name the file was uploaded under

path.description: URL of the stored file. Send it with `id` as a post's media

alt.description: Alt text, when one was set

status.description: A video (MP4 or MOV) is normalized in the background and starts as `processing`; poll `GET /media/{id}/status` until it is `ready` before you put it on a post. Images are `ready` at once.

image.description: Media for this entry. Required: send `[]` for a text-only entry

Only use "UPLOAD" when the user explicitly asks to review or edit the post inside the TikTok app before publishing. "UPLOAD" also makes TikTok ignore every other setting in this object except the title.

eventTitle.description: Event or offer title (required for EVENT and OFFER)

eventStartDate.description: Start date, YYYY-MM-DD (required for EVENT and OFFER)

eventEndDate.description: End date, YYYY-MM-DD (required for EVENT and OFFER)

url.description: Optional link URL to include in the post

post_type.description: Post to the Page feed (default) or as a Page story

text_format_preset_id.description: Background preset for a short text-only post

hasMore.description: Whether there are more pages available

link.description: Optional link associated with the notification

url.description: Thumbnail or preview URL for the content

percentageChange.description: Not computed today: each network sends a fixed `0` or `5`. Ignore it.

average.description: When `true`, the figure for the range is the average of the days, not their sum. Set on daily rates and daily unique counts, such as engagement rate and average daily reach.

unit.description: How to show an averaged series. Absent on series that are summed.

tags.description: Optional comma-separated tags, up to 4096 characters

engagementRate.description: (reactions + comments) / impressions x 100, when all three are known
